verdict.rationale: Logseq's own docs say sync is chosen per graph, so a graph can stay local-only without the vendor's cloud. This satisfies the story's 'local-only mode' branch, and community users confirm local data with no mandatory subscription. Running it on git or Syncthing works, but those are user workarounds and earn no credit. missing for 10: a documented first-party self-hosted sync backend the developer operates, and in-depth first-party docs on running fully offline (local-only is mentioned only in one sentence of the Sync page).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole system without the vendor's cloud — local-only mode or a self-hosted sync backend I operate myself

citations.quote: Syncing is a choice that is made per graph and thus allows for some graphs to be local only.
no mandatory subscription, local data, and source availability
